mainTopic: Does רב follow רבי יהודה on מוקצה, and which kinds of מוקצה does even רבי שמעון accept?
overview: The גמרא brings a support that רב follows רבי יהודה, who holds there is a prohibition of מוקצה. The support is רב's ruling that a lamp may be placed on a palm tree for שבת but not for יום טוב. It then challenges this from a case where רב allowed moving a נר חנוכה on שבת. It answers that he relied on רבי שמעון only in an emergency (שעת הדחק). Next, ריש לקיש asks רבי יוחנן whether רבי שמעון agrees to מוקצה when a person actively set something aside, like sown wheat or eggs under a hen. רבי יוחנן answers that for רבי שמעון the only מוקצה is something like lamp oil while it burns. A ברייתא about סוכה decorations, shown to follow רבי שמעון, leads the גמרא to clarify that setting something aside for a מצוה is itself enough to make it forbidden. Then שמואל says רבי שמעון's מוקצה applies only to figs and grapes set out to dry. A ברייתא about all drying fruits challenges him, and the גמרא answers that this ברייתא follows רבי יהודה. The amud ends as רבי שמעון בר רבי begins to ask his father רבי a question, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Proof from the palm-tree lamp that רב follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports the view that רב follows רבי יהודה on מוקצה. It points to רב's ruling that one may place a lamp on a palm tree before שבת, but not before יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: It also makes sense that רב holds like רבי יהודה. רב said: you may put a lamp on top of a palm tree for שבת, but not for יום טוב. If רב holds like רבי יהודה, we understand why שבת and יום טוב are different. But if he held like רבי שמעון, what difference would there be between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a support for the claim that רב holds like רבי יהודה, who forbids moving a lamp that was lit for שבת because it is מוקצה. The support is רב's ruling about placing a lamp on a palm tree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using a tree that is attached to the ground is forbidden by the Rabbis on both שבת and יום טוב. On שבת the lamp is מוקצה according to רבי יהודה, so nobody will climb up to take it down, and leaving it there is safe. On יום טוב a lamp may be moved, so a person might reach for it and use the tree. That explains רב's distinction. According to רבי שמעון, the lamp is not מוקצה even on שבת, so the same worry would apply to both days, and רב's distinction would make no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: It is also logical / this is also reasonable (introduces a support)
Palm tree
An item set aside from use, which may not be moved on שבת
It works out well (if you say this)

keyTerms.term: מָה לִי שַׁבָּת וּמָה לִי יוֹם טוֹב
keyTerms.meaning: What difference is there between שבת and יום טוב?

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how a small difference in a ruling (שבת versus יום טוב) can reveal which side of a larger debate a אמורא holds.

phrases.english: So too, it is reasonable
that Rav holds like Rabbi Yehuda,
for Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: מַנִּיחִין נֵר עַל גַּבֵּי דֶּקֶל בְּשַׁבָּת,
phrases.english: One may place a lamp on top of a palm tree for Shabbat,
phrases.notes: The lamp is placed there before שבת begins.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין מַנִּיחִין נֵר עַל גַּבֵּי דֶּקֶל בְּיוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.english: but one may not place a lamp on top of a palm tree for a Festival.
Granted, if you say
that Rav holds like Rabbi Yehuda,

phrases.aramaic: הַיְינוּ דְּשָׁנֵי בֵּין שַׁבָּת לְיוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.english: that is why there is a difference between Shabbat and a Festival.
phrases.notes: On שבת the lamp is מוקצה, so one will not come to take it down from the tree.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סְבִירָא לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: But if you say he holds like Rabbi Shimon,

phrases.aramaic: מָה לִי שַׁבָּת וּמָה לִי יוֹם טוֹב?
phrases.english: what difference is there to me between Shabbat and a Festival?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי נָמֵי מִיסְתַּבְּרָא דְּרַב כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה סְבִירָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion, on the previous amud, about רב's position on מוקצה.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that רב holds like רבי יהודה, who forbids moving מוקצה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's ruling that a lamp may be placed on a palm tree for שבת but not for יום טוב.

steps.title: Challenge: רב allowed moving a חנוכה lamp on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that רב holds like רבי יהודה. רב permitted moving a lit נר חנוכה on שבת to hide it from the חברי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רב really hold like רבי יהודה? They once asked רב whether one may move a חנוכה lamp on שבת to hide it from the חברי, and he told them it is fine!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions whether רב truly holds like רבי יהודה. It points to a case where רב allowed moving a burning lamp on שבת, which sounds like רבי שמעון's lenient view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יהודה, a lamp lit for שבת is מוקצה and may not be moved. The חברי were Persian fire-priests who forbade lighting fires on certain days, so people needed to hide their חנוכה lamps. רב's permission to move the lamp seems to show that he does not hold of this type of מוקצה.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so that (introduces a contradiction)
To move or carry an object
A חנוכה lamp
Persian Zoroastrian fire-priests
It is fine / permitted

phrases.english: And does Rav really hold like Rabbi Yehuda?
But didn't they ask Rav:
What is the law about moving a Hanukkah lamp
away from the Ḥabarei on Shabbat?
phrases.notes: The חברי were fire-priests who did not allow lighting fires on certain days.

phrases.english: And he said to them: It is fine!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה סְבִירָא לֵיהּ? וְהָא בְּעוֹ מִינֵּיהּ דְּרַב
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רב holds like רבי יהודה on מוקצה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב allowed moving a burning lamp on שבת. Under רבי יהודה that lamp would be מוקצה, so the permission seems to fit only רבי שמעון.

steps.title: Answer: An emergency is different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב's permission was given only because of the emergency situation.
steps.simpleTranslation: A time of emergency is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the claim that רב holds like רבי יהודה. It explains that the חנוכה case was a special emergency.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being caught by the חברי was dangerous, so רב relied on the lenient view only for that situation. His normal ruling still follows רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: A time of pressing need or emergency
Is different

phrases.english: A time of emergency is different.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case: the ruling was an emergency exception.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's permission shows he holds like רבי שמעון in all cases.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב holds like רבי יהודה normally, and relied on רבי שמעון only in an emergency.

steps.title: Proof that רב relied on רבי שמעון only in an emergency
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves the answer from רב's own words: רבי שמעון is worthy to rely on in an emergency.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רב כהנא and רב אשי asked רב: Is that the law? He told them: רבי שמעון is worthy to rely on in a time of emergency.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings evidence for its answer. When רב was asked whether this was the real law, he said he relied on רבי שמעון only because of the emergency.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's statement shows that he does not normally follow רבי שמעון. If he did, he would not have needed the emergency as a reason. This confirms the תירוץ in Step 3.

keyTerms.meaning: Is this the law?
He is worthy
To rely on him

steps.whatToRemember: רב holds like רבי יהודה on מוקצה. He relied on רבי שמעון's lenient view only in a time of emergency (שעת הדחק).
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic source for the idea that a minority or lenient view may be relied on in a time of emergency (כדאי הוא רבי שמעון לסמוך עליו בשעת הדחק).

phrases.aramaic: דְּהָא אֲמַרוּ לְהוּ רַב כָּהֲנָא וְרַב אָשֵׁי לְרַב:
phrases.english: For Rav Kahana and Rav Ashi said to Rav:
Is that the law?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: כְּדַי הוּא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לִסְמוֹךְ עָלָיו
phrases.english: He said to them: Rabbi Shimon is worthy to rely upon
in a time of emergency.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּהָא אֲמַרוּ לְהוּ רַב כָּהֲנָא וְרַב אָשֵׁי לְרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer given in Step 3.
steps.raayaObject: The answer that רב permitted moving the lamp only because of the emergency.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's reply to רב כהנא and רב אשי.

steps.title: ריש לקיש asks about items a person actively set aside
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש asks רבי יוחנן whether רבי שמעון would agree to מוקצה when a person actively set an item aside with his own hands, such as sown wheat or eggs placed under a hen.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש asked רבי יוחנן: What about wheat a person sowed in the ground, and eggs placed under a hen? Maybe רבי שמעון rejects מוקצה only when the person did not push the item away with his own hands, but when he did, רבי שמעון agrees it is מוקצה. Or maybe there is no difference?
steps.whatsHappening: A new discussion opens. ריש לקיש asks whether רבי שמעון's lenient view on מוקצה has a limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By sowing wheat or placing eggs to hatch, a person actively removed them from normal use. The question is whether this physical act, called דחייה בידים, makes the item מוקצה even for רבי שמעון. The other possibility is that רבי שמעון makes no distinction at all.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him (a question of uncertain law)
He pushed it away with his own hands (actively set it aside)
Hen
Or perhaps there is no difference

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מֵרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Reish Lakish asked Rabbi Yoḥanan:
Wheat kernels that one sowed in the ground,
phrases.notes: They have not yet taken root, so they could still be gathered.

phrases.english: and eggs placed beneath a hen, what is the law?

phrases.aramaic: כִּי לֵית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מוּקְצֶה —
phrases.english: When does Rabbi Shimon not hold of muktze?
Where one did not push it away with his hands;

phrases.aramaic: הֵיכָא דְּדַחְיֵיהּ בְּיָדַיִם — אִית לֵיהּ מוּקְצֶה,
phrases.english: but where he pushed it away with his hands, he does hold of muktze;
or perhaps there is no difference.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מֵרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רב's position to defining the limits of רבי שמעון's view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רבי שמעון agree that an item is מוקצה when a person actively set it aside with his own hands?

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: The only מוקצה for רבי שמעון is burning oil
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that רבי שמעון holds of מוקצה only for oil burning in a lamp. That oil is set aside both for its מצוה and because touching it involves a prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: רבי שמעון has no מוקצה except the oil in a lamp while it is burning. Since it was set aside for its מצוה, it is also set aside because of its prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers that active setting-aside does not make something מוקצה for רבי שמעון. Only burning lamp oil is מוקצה for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wheat and eggs are therefore permitted according to רבי שמעון. Burning oil is special because two things combine: it is set aside for the מצוה of the שבת lamp (הוקצה למצותו), and moving it risks putting out the flame (הוקצה לאיסורו).

keyTerms.meaning: The oil that is in the lamp
Since
Set aside for its מצוה
Set aside because of its prohibition

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן's answer is not saying that sown wheat is not seed, or that the eggs are not set aside. It says that for רבי שמעון, the act of setting something aside does not by itself create the מוקצה prohibition.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֵין מוּקְצֶה לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
phrases.english: He said to him: There is no muktze according to Rabbi Shimon

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא שֶׁמֶן שֶׁבַּנֵּר בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁהוּא דּוֹלֵק,
phrases.english: except the oil in the lamp while it is burning,
since it was set aside for its מצוה,
it was also set aside for its prohibition.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֵין מוּקְצֶה לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אֶלָּא שֶׁמֶן שֶׁבַּנֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers ריש לקיש's question in Step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No difference: active setting-aside does not create מוקצה for רבי שמעון. Only burning lamp oil is מוקצה, because it is set aside both for a מצוה and because of a prohibition.

steps.title: Challenge from סוכה decorations
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that a מצוה setting-aside alone does not create מוקצה. It cites a ברייתא forbidding use of סוכה decorations for the entire festival.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does he not hold that being set aside for a מצוה is enough? But a ברייתא teaches: If someone roofed a סוכה properly and decorated it with colored hangings and decorated sheets, and hung in it nuts, peaches, almonds, pomegranates, grape clusters, wreaths of grain stalks, wines, oils, and fine flour, he may not take anything from them until the end of the last day of the festival. If he made a condition about them, everything follows his condition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's statement that something set aside only for a מצוה is not מוקצה for רבי שמעון. Steps 8–9 first confirm that this ברייתא follows רבי שמעון, and Step 10 answers the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן implied that being set aside for a מצוה alone (הוקצה למצותו) is not enough without a prohibition attached. The ברייתא about סוכה decorations involves no prohibition like putting out a flame. Still, it forbids using the decorations only because they were set aside for the מצוה of סוכה. The גמרא assumes this ruling applies even according to רבי שמעון, so it seems to contradict רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא?
He roofed the סוכה according to its law (with proper סכך)
To take or use from them
He made a condition (stipulated)

phrases.english: And does he not hold that something set aside for its מצוה is muktze?
But wasn't it taught: If one roofed the sukka properly
and decorated it with colored hangings and decorated sheets,

phrases.aramaic: וְתָלָה בָּהּ אֱגוֹזִין, אֲפַרְסְקִין, שְׁקֵדִים וְרִמּוֹנִין,
phrases.english: and hung in it nuts, peaches, almonds, and pomegranates,
and grape clusters, and wreaths of grain stalks,
wines, oils, and fine flour,
it is forbidden to take from them
until the end of the last day of the Festival.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם הִתְנָה עֲלֵיהֶן — הַכֹּל לְפִי תְנָאוֹ.
phrases.english: And if he stipulated about them, all is according to his stipulation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי יוחנן's answer in Step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's statement that רבי שמעון holds of מוקצה only when an item is set aside both for a מצוה and because of a prohibition.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא forbids using סוכה decorations only because they were set aside for a מצוה, with no prohibition involved. This suggests that הוקצה למצותו alone is enough to make something forbidden.

steps.title: How do we know the סוכה-decorations ברייתא follows רבי שמעון?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know that the ברייתא forbidding סוכה decorations follows רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know that this ברייתא follows רבי שמעון?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from Step 7 does not name its author. The גמרא now asks how we know it follows רבי שמעון, and this sets up the proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge in Step 7 only works if the decorations ברייתא matches רבי שמעון's view. If it followed רבי יהודה, who holds of מוקצה broadly, it would not contradict רבי יוחנן at all. So the גמרא must show that the ruling belongs to רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: From where? How do we know?
The תנא who is generally lenient about מוקצה
'It is', meaning the ברייתא is his view

phrases.english: And from where do we know that it is Rabbi Shimon's view?
phrases.notes: This is about the ברייתא on סוכה decorations from Step 7, which doesn't say whose view it is.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the basis of the assumption behind the Step 7 challenge.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What shows that the anonymous decorations ברייתא follows רבי שמעון?

steps.title: Even רבי שמעון forbids the wood of the festival סוכה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי שמעון permits wood from an ordinary סוכה on יום טוב but agrees that the סוכה built for the festival of סוכות is forbidden all festival.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר יוסף taught before רבי יוחנן: one may not take wood from a סוכה on יום טוב, only from the pile next to it, and רבי שמעון permits. Both agree that the festival סוכה is forbidden during the festival. If one made a condition about it, everything follows his condition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא showing that even רבי שמעון forbids using a סוכת החג during the festival.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון normally rejects מוקצה, so he allows wood from an ordinary shade סוכה. Yet he still forbids the festival סוכה, and the only reason is that it was set aside for a מצוה. That matches the decorations ברייתא, so that ruling can belong to רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: One takes
Wood, sticks (for fuel)
What is next to it (wood piled beside the סוכה, not part of it)
The סוכה built for the festival of סוכות, a מצוה סוכה
He made a condition (stated in advance that he may use it)
His condition

steps.confusionAlert: There are two kinds of סוכה here. The first line is about an ordinary shade סוכה on any יום טוב, and רבי שמעון permits its wood. The 'agreement' line is about the מצוה סוכה of סוכות, which even רבי שמעון forbids.

phrases.english: For Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Yosef taught
before Rabbi Yoḥanan:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין נוֹטְלִין עֵצִים מִן הַסּוּכָּה בְּיוֹם טוֹב
phrases.english: One may not take wood from the sukka on a Festival
phrases.notes: An ordinary shade סוכה, which may not be taken apart on יום טוב.

phrases.english: but only from what is beside it.
And Rabbi Shimon permits it.
phrases.notes: He generally does not hold of מוקצה.

phrases.aramaic: וְשָׁוִין בְּסוּכַּת הַחַג בֶּחָג שֶׁהִיא אֲסוּרָה,
phrases.english: And they agree that the festival sukka is forbidden during the festival,
and if he made a condition about it,
everything follows his condition.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתָנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר יוֹסֵף קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 8 by showing that רבי שמעון forbids מצוה-designated סוכה material.
steps.raayaObject: That the decorations ברייתא can follow רבי שמעון
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי חייא בר יוסף: 'וְשָׁוִין בְּסוּכַּת הַחַג בֶּחָג שֶׁהִיא אֲסוּרָה'

steps.title: Correcting רבי יוחנן's rule: a מצוה setting-aside is enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא revises רבי יוחנן's statement: מוקצה applies to anything like the lamp oil, because being set aside for a מצוה is itself enough to make something forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: We meant 'something similar to oil in the lamp': since it was set aside for its מצוה, it was set aside for its prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the challenge and rewords רבי יוחנן's rule from Step 6.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 suggested that two reasons were needed, the מצוה and the ban on touching the burning oil. The revised version says one reason is enough: once something is set aside for a מצוה, that alone makes it forbidden. This fits both the lamp oil and the סוכה decorations.

keyTerms.meaning: Similar to, of the same type as
We are saying, we meant
Since
It was set aside for its מצוה
It is (thereby) set aside as forbidden

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'הוֹאִיל וְהוּקְצָה לְמִצְוָתוֹ הוּקְצָה לְאִיסּוּרוֹ' as listing two separate reasons. Here it means the מצוה setting-aside itself causes the prohibition.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets the final rule for רבי שמעון according to רבי יוחנן: he holds of מוקצה for things set aside for a מצוה, such as the festival סוכה and its decorations.

phrases.english: We meant: something similar to oil in the lamp,
since it was set aside for its מצוה,
it was set aside for its prohibition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the Step 7 challenge, now confirmed by Step 9, by revising רבי יוחנן's wording.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rewording or emending the earlier statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון holds of מוקצה only when there is both a מצוה and a separate prohibition, as with burning oil.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי שמעון, a מצוה setting-aside alone creates מוקצה, as with the lamp oil.

steps.title: Another report of רבי יוחנן confirms the corrected wording
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא reports רבי יוחנן's statement in exactly the corrected form.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also stated: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: for רבי שמעון there is מוקצה only in a case like oil in the lamp while it burns, since it was set aside for its מצוה it was set aside for its prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a separate report of רבי יוחנן's words that matches the corrected version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The correction in Step 10 is not just a guess made to escape the challenge. Another student heard רבי יוחנן say it with the word 'כעין', meaning 'like the oil'. That makes the rule broader than the oil case alone.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also stated (an independent report that supports what was just said)
The אמורא who transmits רבי יוחנן's teaching
While it is burning

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוחנן, רבי שמעון holds of מוקצה for things set aside for a מצוה, like lamp oil while it burns, and the festival סוכה with its decorations.

phrases.english: It was also stated:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
There is no set-aside according to Rabbi Shimon
except in a case like oil in the lamp
while it is burning;
since it was set aside for its מצוה,
it was set aside for its prohibition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the corrected wording of Step 10 with a separate report.
steps.raayaObject: The corrected version of רבי יוחנן's rule
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי חייא בר אבא's report of רבי יוחנן

steps.title: שמואל: for רבי שמעון, מוקצה applies only to dried figs and raisins
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה reports in the name of שמואל that רבי שמעון holds of מוקצה only for figs and grapes set out to dry.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: for רבי שמעון there is מוקצה only with dried figs and raisins.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new view from שמואל about the limits of רבי שמעון's מוקצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Figs and grapes put on the roof to dry are inedible for a while, so a person clearly gives up on them. שמואל says this is the only case where רבי שמעון forbids something as מוקצה. This opens a new line of discussion.

keyTerms.meaning: Dried figs (figs set out to dry)
Raisins (grapes set out to dry)
Only, alone
The early בבלי אמורא whose statement this is

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
There is no set-aside according to Rabbi Shimon
except dried figs and raisins alone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new view on the scope of רבי שמעון's מוקצה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For רבי שמעון, מוקצה applies only to figs and grapes set out to dry.

steps.title: A ברייתא forbids all fruits set out to dry
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל with a ברייתא that applies the drying rule to peaches, quinces, and every other fruit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is nothing else included? But a ברייתא teaches: if someone was eating figs, left some over, and brought them to the roof to dry, or did the same with grapes to make raisins, he may not eat them until he designates them. The same is true for peaches, quinces, and all other fruits.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions שמואל's limit by quoting a ברייתא that covers all kinds of fruit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל limited רבי שמעון's מוקצה to figs and grapes. This ברייתא forbids every fruit set out to dry unless it was designated for eating beforehand. The challenge only works if the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון, which the next step will try to show.

keyTerms.meaning: Something else, another item
But a ברייתא teaches
He left some over
Until he designates (sets them aside for eating before שבת)
Peaches
Quinces

phrases.english: And nothing else is included?
But it was taught in a baraita:
If one was eating figs and left some over
and took them up to the roof to make dried figs from them,
or was eating grapes and left some over
and took them up to the roof to make raisins from them,
he may not eat them unless he designates them.
And so you say
with regard to peaches and quinces
and all other kinds of fruit.

steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's claim that רבי שמעון holds of מוקצה only for גרוגרות and צימוקים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא extends the drying-fruit prohibition to all fruits, which would be broader than שמואל allowed.

steps.title: The fruit ברייתא must follow רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues the ברייתא cannot follow רבי יהודה, since for him the ruling would be obvious. So it must follow רבי שמעון, which contradicts שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? If you say רבי יהודה: he holds of מוקצה even where the person did not push the item away with his own hands, so where he did, all the more so. It must be רבי שמעון!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא works out who wrote the ברייתא, and this completes the challenge against שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה forbids מוקצה even when the person did nothing active. A case where the person actively carried fruit to the roof would then be too obvious to teach. So the ברייתא must be רבי שמעון's, and that means רבי שמעון includes all fruits, against שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view is it?
If you say
He pushed it away with his own hands (actively set it aside)
All the more so
Rather, is it not...? (pushes toward the only remaining option)

phrases.english: Whose view is it?
If you say it is Rabbi Yehuda,
if where he did not push it away with his hands
he holds there is set-aside,
then where he pushed it away with his hands,
is it not all the more so?
Rather, is it not Rabbi Shimon's view!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the Step 13 challenge by identifying the ברייתא as רבי שמעון's.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's limit of רבי שמעון's מוקצה to figs and grapes
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For רבי יהודה the ruling would be a needless כל שכן, so the ברייתא must be רבי שמעון's. It includes all fruits, which contradicts שמואל.

steps.title: The ברייתא follows רבי יהודה; its new point is the case of someone in the middle of eating
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה. It was needed because the person was in the middle of eating, and we might have thought no designation was needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really it is רבי יהודה, and the eating case is why it was needed. You might have thought that since he was in the middle of eating, he needs no designation. So it teaches us that once he brought them up to the roof, he took his mind off them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the challenge. The ברייתא can follow רבי יהודה because it teaches something new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new point is the case of someone who was in the middle of eating the fruit. We might think his mind is still on the leftovers. The ברייתא teaches that carrying them to the roof shows he gave up on them, so שמואל's view of רבי שמעון stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually, really (keeping the original option)
It was needed (to teach a new point)
It would have entered your mind to say (the mistaken assumption)
Designation (setting aside for eating before שבת)
It teaches us
He fully took his mind off it

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's rule survives. The fruit ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, and its new point is that even someone in the middle of eating gives up on fruit once he puts it on the roof to dry.

phrases.english: Actually, it is Rabbi Yehuda,
and the case of one who was eating was needed.
It would have entered your mind to say
that since he was in the middle of eating,
he does not need designation.
So it teaches us
that since he brought them up to the roof,
he fully took his mind off them.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, וְאוֹכֵל אִצְטְרִיכָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects Step 14's conclusion that the ברייתא must be רבי שמעון's, which saves שמואל.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the ברייתא by finding a new point in the case (the 'eating' detail)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Someone in the middle of eating keeps his mind on the leftovers, so no designation is needed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Bringing the fruit to the roof shows he fully gave up on it, so even for רבי יהודה the ברייתא teaches something new.

steps.title: רבי שמעון son of רבי asks his father a question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new source on the same topic. רבי שמעון בר רבי asks a question of his father, רבי. The actual question follows in the next line.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון, the son of רבי, asked רבי a question:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is introducing a question that רבי שמעון בר רבי asked his father רבי, and the content of the question comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words בעא מיניה tell us a real question, a בעיא, is about to be asked. It is not an attack. The גמרא is bringing a new voice into the discussion about how far רבי שמעון's rule on מוקצה reaches. The question and its answer will help settle the issue raised by שמואל's statement.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked of him, the standard opening for a sincere question put to a teacher
רבי שמעון, son of רבי יהודה הנשיא
רבי יהודה הנשיא, the editor of the משנה, called simply 'רבי'

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רבי שמעון בר רבי, רבי's son who is asking here, with the תנא רבי שמעון (בר יוחאי), whose view on מוקצה is being discussed. They are two different people.

phrases.english: Asked of him
Rabbi Shimon son of Rabbi, of Rabbi:
phrases.notes: The son asks his father, רבי יהודה הנשיא

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בַּר רַבִּי מֵרַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the challenge to שמואל was answered in Step 15, the גמרא brings a related question on the same topic: how far רבי שמעון's view on מוקצה extends.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The question has not been stated yet. This line only introduces who is asking and whom he asks. The content comes in the next line.
